name: restrained-strip-transient-thermal-stress
reference: Benchmark E8 (transient field chaining, #84). A plane-stress strip (1 m x 0.2 m, 0.2 m thick) is restrained on every edge (ux = uy = 0) and stepped from T0 = 300 K to T1 = 400 K at both x-faces by a heat-transient Step (diffusivity k/(rho cp) = 1 m^2/s); the static Step named after it is solved once per retained frame (#84), keeping the last as its Result and a von Mises frame per output time. The temperature is the same Fourier sine series the cooled-slab transient benchmark (E5 in docs/BENCHMARKS.md) uses, generalised to a rise between two endpoints instead of a decay to zero; using 50 terms, the omitted tail is exponentially negligible at every checked time. The stress is sigma_xx = sigma_yy = -E alpha dT / (1 - nu): the plane-STRESS biaxial-restraint result (sigma_zz = 0, free through the thickness), not the plane-STRAIN one -- a fully restrained plane-strain strip has zero strain in all three normal directions too, so it is the classical *confined* thermal stress sigma_xx = sigma_yy = sigma_zz = -E alpha dT / (1 - 2 nu), which is hydrostatic and carries zero von Mises everywhere. Per-frame min/max are gated against the analytic extremes at 1% of the E alpha (T1-T0) / (1-nu) = 300 MPa scale; the final frame is gated pointwise at 1e-6 relative, because by t = 2 s (about 20 diffusion time constants) the field is uniform to far below that.
